name: Rijksmuseum
description: The national museum of the Netherlands. Vermeer, Rembrandt, and Delftware at a scale that takes a full day to absorb.
notes: Arrived early to avoid the crowds. Spent two hours in the Gallery of Honour alone.

name: Anne Frank House
description: The canal house where Anne Frank and her family hid during WWII. A profoundly moving experience.
notes: Book tickets months in advance. The original diary pages on display are unforgettable.

name: Markthal Rotterdam
description: An extraordinary arch-shaped building combining a fresh food market with 228 apartments. The interior ceiling mural is stunning.
notes: Go at lunchtime. The stroopwafel stall near the entrance is worth the queue.

name: Senso-ji Temple
description: Tokyo's oldest and most significant temple. Located in Asakusa — the area retains more of old Tokyo than anywhere else.
notes: Visit at dawn before the crowds arrive. The incense smoke and lanterns at first light are extraordinary.

name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
description: A dense corridor of bamboo stalks towering 30 meters overhead. The sound of the wind moving through them is singular.
notes: Crowded by 9am. Arrive at 6:30am. Combine with Tenryu-ji garden next door.

name: Torre de Belem
description: A 16th-century fortified tower on the Tagus river — a symbol of Portugal's Age of Discovery and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
notes: The interior is atmospheric but cramped. The exterior from the water is the real spectacle.

name: Livraria Lello
description: One of the most beautiful bookshops in the world. A neo-Gothic masterpiece with a crimson staircase and stained glass ceiling.
notes: Buy a book — the ticket price is refunded against a purchase. Crowded but worth it.
